title: Example 122: a cache expiry in milliseconds left expires entries in their last millisecond, found under the stated relation
description: Regression proof (B9) of Crosscut's cache expiry between the committed version, Expiry#isExpired returning a boolean, and the patched one, Expiry#remainingMillis returning the milliseconds an entry has left, with the relation between the results stated as previousArguments-style metadata: resultsAgreeWhen 'previous == (result <= 0)' (the new --results-agree-when of jvmcontract equivalence, lib/src/harness/mod.rs and lib/src/equivalence.rs), the previous method named by previousSymbol, and the scope the module's own precondition. Expected: a counterexample with a fraction of a millisecond to go, such as remainingMillis(writtenAtNanos=0, ttlNanos=1, nowNanos=0), before false and after 0, with the line 'the results are not related by previous == (result <= 0)'. The library's test of the same shape finds it in about a second. The job runs build.py on the example, which compiles both Crosscut trees with javac and runs jvmcontract equivalence with the relation.
expected: Verdict violation; a counterexample inside the precondition, before false and after 0, and the example's result.json records it

resources.notes: the last run used a stale jvmcontract; measured by the submitting sessions in seconds at under 200 MiB, except 142 at bound 8, 7 s
